tasks.q: Which of these is systems software?
tasks.fb: Systems software runs the machine; applications run on top of it.

tasks.q: Is each program systems software or application software?
tasks.fb: If it looks after the computer, it's systems software. If it does a job for the user, it's an application.

tasks.q: Which of these are jobs of an operating system? Select all that apply.
tasks.fb: The OS runs the machine. It doesn't do the user's work, and it doesn't build the hardware.

tasks.q: Why does an application not talk to the hardware directly?
a: The OS handles the hardware, so the same program runs on very different machines
Applications are not allowed to use memory
tasks.fb: That's why a browser works on machines with completely different processors and printers.

tasks.q: What is the main advantage of a GUI?
a: It is easy to learn, because you can see the options
It is faster for experts to automate
tasks.fb: You don't have to remember any commands.

tasks.q: What is the main disadvantage of a GUI?
a: It uses more memory and processing power
tasks.fb: Drawing all those windows costs resources.

tasks.q: Why do network managers often use a command line?
a: Commands can be scripted, so the same job runs on hundreds of machines
tasks.fb: One script can do in seconds what would take hours of clicking.

tasks.q: What is the main drawback of a command line interface?
a: The user has to know the commands
tasks.fb: There is nothing on screen to prompt you.

tasks.q: Match each situation to the most suitable interface.
pairs: A tablet for a young child
A smart speaker in a kitchen
tasks.fb: Match the interface to the user and the situation, not to what you like best.

tasks.q: What is a drawback of a voice interface?
a: Background noise and accents can cause it to mishear
It can't be used hands free
tasks.fb: It also struggles with anything that has to be precise, like a long file name.

tasks.q: Which is the best exam answer for a supermarket self-service till?
a: A menu driven interface, because shoppers need no training and only a few choices are allowed
A GUI, because it looks nicer
A CLI, because it is fastest

tasks.q: A computer in a server room has no monitor attached. Which interface is most suitable?
Which interface suits each device best?
items: A laptop used by a Year 7 class
A web server managed from another building
A ticket machine at a station
A hands-free system in a car
Automating a nightly backup on 200 machines
tasks.fb: The user and the situation decide, every time.

info.title: Where the name comes from
info.text: Early computers ran one job at a time, loaded by hand. The first 'operating systems' were programs that loaded the next job automatically, so the operator didn't have to.

info.title: Bigger than you think
info.text: A modern operating system is tens of millions of lines of code, and is being updated somewhere in the world every day.

info.title: Xerox first
info.text: The windows, icons and pointer idea was developed at Xerox PARC in the 1970s, before either Apple or Microsoft shipped a graphical system.

info.title: The command line never died
info.text: Most servers, cloud platforms and developer tools are still driven from a command line, because a typed command can be repeated exactly and stored in a script.

info.title: Interfaces for access
info.text: Voice control, screen readers and switch devices are interfaces too. Choosing the right one can be the difference between a computer being usable or useless to someone.

info.title: Embedded systems
info.text: The washing machine from topic 1.1 has an operating system too, but a tiny one, with a menu driven interface of dials and buttons.

models.title: The software stack
models.text: Pull the layers apart: hardware at the bottom, the operating system in the middle, applications on top.

models.title: What sits where
models.text: Every request from an application goes through the operating system before it reaches the hardware.
